FIELD FACTS · PHOTO GUIDELINES
  • Smile, greet people, and ask before taking a portrait.
  • Dress modestly at the Temple of Literature and sacred sites.
  • Cross streets at a steady pace. Do not step backward.
  • White or cream linen complements Old Quarter ochre.
  • Stay safe: never step onto active railway tracks.

TRAVELFRAME · FIELD TIMELINE · DIURNAL CYCLE
TRACKING SUNLIGHT AND SHADOW, 05:45-20:30.
[ 24-HOUR FIELD ITINERARY ]
✦
FROM DAWN'S STILLNESS TO THE NIGHT'S ENERGY.
FROM DAWN UNTIL THE BLUE HOUR.
05:45 – 07:15
THE AWAKENING · HOAN KIEM AT DAWN
Low angled light, a veil of mist over the lake, and long shadows. Elderly locals practice tai chi beneath trailing willow branches.
Camera angle: Shoot west from the eastern shore toward Turtle Tower in soft backlight. Get low to catch reflections. Use 35mm/50mm at f/2.0.
Breakfast: Stir-fried rare-beef pho at Pho Thin (13 Lo Duc) or steamed rice rolls at Ba Hoanh (66 To Hien Thanh). Backlight the rising steam.
07:45 – 09:30
STREET TEXTURES · DONG XUAN ALLEYS & OLD QUARTER
Sunbeams cut through narrow tube-house gaps. Look for charcoal smoke, flower vendors, the Phung Hung railway arches, and 47 Hang Bac.
Camera angle: Use at least 1/250s to freeze drifting smoke. Look up for Indochine iron balconies. Always smile and ask vendors before photographing them.
10:00 – 12:00
MIDDAY PAUSE · HERITAGE CAFE INTERLUDE
Escape the harsh overhead sun in a cool interior: Cafe Dinh (second floor, 13 Dinh Tien Hoang) or Cafe Giang (39 Nguyen Huu Huan).
Camera angle: Use diffused natural window light. Capture a close-up of silky egg-coffee foam on a rustic wooden table.
13:30 – 15:30
HERITAGE SYMMETRY · TEMPLE & FRENCH QUARTER
Explore the Temple of Literature's five symmetrical courtyards and red Khuê Van Pavilion, or the elegant Trang Tien boulevard and Opera House.
Camera angle: Build frames within frames through round doorways and ironwood columns. Use precise symmetry to make the subject stand out.
16:00 – 17:45
CINEMATIC SUNSET · LONG BIEN BRIDGE
Honeyed afternoon light crosses the 1902 Daydé & Pillé steel beams above green banana fields on the Red River banks.
Camera angle: Use side light for a glowing rim. A telephoto lens compresses cyclists and trains. Stay firmly in the pedestrian lane and never climb onto the tracks.
18:15 – 20:30
BLUE HOUR & NIGHT · OLD QUARTER & HANG MA
A deep blue sky contrasts with Hang Ma's red lanterns and the lively plastic stools around Ta Hien intersection.
Camera angle: Open to f/1.8-f/2.8 and raise ISO to 1600-3200. Capture motorbike light trails and warm light on faces along the sidewalk.

OPTICAL SPECS · LENS GUIDE
35MM PRIME (F/1.8-2.8): The street-photography sweet spot. Capture narrow alleys and daily life without distorting the scene.
50MM PRIME (F/1.8): Natural environmental portraits with gentle subject separation against weathered ochre walls.
85MM TELEPHOTO: Compress perspective beautifully on Long Bien Bridge and isolate ornate ironwork on upper balconies.
CPL FILTER: Reduce glare on Hoan Kiem Lake and deepen Hanoi's autumn-blue skies.

THE FOUR VISUAL MOODS CURATED BY TRAVELFRAME
HERITAGE HANOI
Indochine balconies, deep alleys, mossy yin-yang roof tiles, and century-old ochre walls.
EVERYDAY HANOI

Recommended clothing: Natural fabrics such as linen, cotton, or silk in white, cream, beige, pastel blue, or a traditional ao dai. Avoid bright neon and oversized logos.
Footwear: Old Quarter sidewalks are uneven, so choose flats or comfortable sneakers.
PHOTOGRAPHER'S CODE (V-09)
1. SMILE AND GREET: Never push a lens into a stranger's face. Smile and ask politely: "Hello, may I take a photo of you?"
2. RESPECT SACRED SPACES: Cover shoulders and knees at the Temple of Literature and Tran Quoc Pagoda. Do not pose with your back to an altar.
3. STAY SAFE AND AWARE: Cross at a steady pace so motorbikes can flow around you; agree on a cyclo fare before riding; never stand on active railway tracks.
